A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same angular-calibration and Platt-scaling study. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gaussian, Rademacher, and uniform-design simulations in Figures 1–4, including calibration results and Monte Carlo sign-estimation outcomes.

after.justification: V2 retains those simulations and adds original experiments using real covariates with simulated labels, reported in Tables 1–2 and Appendix H.2.

M1.justification: The binary procedure is retained, but Section 8 and Appendix F introduce a multi-index angular predictor using a matrix-valued conditional mean and Gaussian residual covariance. This substantially extends the predictor's inputs and outputs, although the required cross-index angle estimators remain undeveloped.

E1.justification: Section 7.2 adds covariates from CIFAR-10, 20 Newsgroups, Tox21, Communities & Crime, Splice-junction Gene Sequences, and Madelon, using pretrained representations or raw features. Labels remain simulated binary outcomes. The original synthetic-design coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add isotonic calibration, labeled Iso, with 100 and 500 holdout observations. V1 evaluates angular calibration against Platt scaling and uncalibrated predictions; these comparators remain in v2.

E3.justification: The new experiments introduce true-angle evaluation, covariance estimation from separate unlabeled pools, dataset-specific sample sizes and feature dimensions, and ECE reporting. Platt and Iso use 100 or 500 labeled holdout observations. These are additional protocols; the original simulation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 7.2 adds a qualitative diagnostic finding that the plug-in angle estimator is unstable on real covariates, motivating evaluation with true angles to isolate calibration effects. No quantitative estimator ablation accompanies this finding. The existing holdout-size, non-Gaussian-design, and link-function analyses remain in Figures 1–4.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 5000 Monte Carlo trials for sign estimation. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its new ECE results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Appendix H.2 add results for six semi-real settings. For example, CIFAR-10 has oracle Angular ECE 0.0199; Communities & Crime has Angular 0.0296 and Platt 500 0.0262. These are newly reported results under the oracle protocol, not matched v1 performance improvements. Original simulation values and Figures 1–4 are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds Theorem F.1 and a proof of calibration for the multi-index construction using Gaussian conditioning. Section 8 also adds a mathematical universality argument with explicit covariance and moment conditions, while deferring a formal non-Gaussian proof. The original binary theorems and proofs are substantially retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal contribution claims remain unchanged. The final section now claims an explicit multi-index calibration construction, whereas v1 only proposed broader models and multiclass calibration as future directions; practical angle estimation remains qualified as future work.

C2.justification: V2 newly discloses angle-estimator instability on real covariates and attributes it to the estimator's design assumptions. It consequently limits the new experiments to simulated labels and true angles. Section 8 and Appendix F also identify unavailable cross-index angle estimators as a barrier to applying the extension.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds end-to-end pseudocode, explicitly documenting cosine clipping and Monte Carlo approximation of the Gaussian expectation. Section 7.2 identifies frozen ResNet-34, MiniLM, and ChemBERTa representations and raw-covariate linear heads. The original binary estimation formulas were already documented.

R1.justification: V2 expands supporting references for multi-index models, CLT and AMP universality, isotonic regression, and the added datasets and feature extractors. Examples include Bruna and Hsu, Troiani et al., Bentkus, and Chen and Lam. The central research-gap and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. Section 7 becomes Numerical experiments with simulation and semi-real subsections; Section 8 is retitled and expanded. References move before the appendices, and theorem numbering and internal references are revised.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different document template, changing the title and author block, typography, margins, and running headers. It adds two tables, an algorithm display, and six reliability panels. Figures 3–4 move to Appendix H.1; their underlying plot content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves usability and transparency through Algorithm 1, broader controlled experiments, and explicit disclosure of angle-estimator instability. The gains are limited: the new results use simulated labels and true angles, uncertainty reporting is unchanged, and the multi-index extension still lacks data-driven cross-angle estimators. The principal binary results remain substantially unchanged.
